title: Q-Bridge: adaptive quantization + batching pilot and rollout log
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Q-Bridge is an experiment-driven initiative to combine lightweight quantization profiles with adaptive batching and prefix/KV prefetch heuristics. Objective: reduce per-token compute costs for common Redwood workloads while keeping user-visible quality regressions under an agreed guardrail. The program couples offline benching, mirrored traffic A/B testing, and an automated rollback policy tied to quality/e2e metrics.
updates: 2025-02-10: Initiative created. Hypothesis: 20-30% cost reduction on text generation and 10-25% for embedding pipelines with localized 0.5-1.5% acceptable quality delta on PR metrics.

2025-02-18: Eng team delivered microbench harness for mixed-precision quant profiles (8-bit, 4-bit simulated) and an initial cost/latency matrix across GPU types. Results attached in linked_artifacts.

2025-02-25: Design and PM aligned on experiment guardrails: max allowed delta on eval suite = 1% relative nLL increase; 99th percentile latency SLO = 350ms for hosted tier. Added rollout plan with mirrored traffic and 1% live canary.
2025-03-01: Engineering spike completed for dynamic batch sizing with latency headroom detection. Canary controller prototype ready; PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6872.

2025-03-05: Data science produced eval dashboard with drift alerts (perplexity, embedding cosine, human-labeled fail rate). Agreed to run first mirrored test with 0.5% traffic on embeddings on 2025-03-12. Next: schedule pilot sign-off meeting and SRE runbook review.
